title: bls12-381-g1-ecdlp-plain: six-class (negation + GLV) parallel Pollard rho in G1, global work meter, truncated-product canonicalisation

claims.statement: For a uniform challenge T=[x]P0 in BLS12-381 G1 (T=infinity returns 0), the algorithm in proof.md outputs x with success probability at least 0.39, and on every run its total work is at most 2^126.36 batched-affine-G1-addition equivalents (C=2,000 instructions), enforced by a global work meter that charges every action at an upper-bound price before execution and halts with failure at 2^126.36. The algorithm is parallel distinguished-point Pollard rho (2^20 walks, distinguished probability 2^-64, trail cap 20*2^64) on the (r-1)/6 classes of G1 under negation and phi(x,y)=(beta*x,y)=[lambda], lambda=0xac45a4010001a40200000000ffffffff; class key |y|; canonical twist index decided exactly from a truncated 12-multiply fixed-point product of x by floor(2^448*beta/p) with an exact one-multiplication fallback on near-ties (a separately metered action; proof.md section 1.1); R=2048 twisted table so each step is one batched affine addition plus at most 200 instructions; 2-cycles and cycles of length <=64 escaped by doubling the minimum-key class (a class map; no cancellation can close a cycle through doublings since the order of 2 mod r is 2^250.86), so trails meeting a common class reunite (merging lemma); fresh uniform trail coefficients stored in full; collisions solved by re-walking with coefficients reduced mod r and x=(e_2-e_1)/(f_1-f_2) mod r verified before output. Phase 1 stops when a hard operation counter reaches S_ops=1.05*S0 (S0=sqrt(2N'ln(1/0.605)), steps priced 1.10 units and doublings 1.5, 1.10*S_ops=2^126.3479, N'=((r-1)/6)*2048/2047); phase 2 completes open trails; report capacity 2^63.25 and 8 processed matches are caps counted as failure. Peak memory below 2^72 bytes; preprocessing (all work before the first walk step: jump table, report-table initialisation, first 2^20 trail starts) at most 2^57.2 units, enforced by a meter sub-cap and included in the total; no advice. Heuristic H1: within S_ops class arrivals of all trails (all arrivals counted, including fruitless-cycle repeats and trail starts) the first inter-trail collision has occurred with probability at least 1-exp(-(S_ops/1.05)^2/(2N'))=0.395 (random-mapping law with a 5% slowdown allowance); the meter's early-halt probability (expected doubling surcharge against the headroom, Markov) is below 0.004, and the |y| bits used for partition and distinguished tests are pseudo-random; beta*x mod p is assumed equidistributed along the walk (this only affects the fallback rate and hence the early-halt probability); supported by toy-curve experiments (including a no-automorphism control and a scaled full-pipeline mode); no production-size run.

experiments.purpose: Part A: on BLS12-381 G1, check the GLV pair, orbit size 6 and unit action, |y| class key, canonical member, the section-1.1 truncated-product canonical index against the exact rule (random and adversarial near-tie inputs), twisted-step identity, doubling class map, the multiplicative order of 2 mod r, table entries, coefficient tracking on production steps, and recovery of a planted x from two production trails forced to merge. Part B: run the per-trail algorithm of proof.md on a toy curve y^2=x^3+4 over F_q and report class visits to the first inter-trail collision against the random-mapping model and fruitless-cycle rates; pipeline=true also applies the scaled production rules (phase-1 budget, phase 2, report capacity, 8-match cap) and reports the success rate; classes=1 or 2 runs control walks. Toy scale only. Optional canon_random/canon_stress set the number of section-1.1 checks; toy=false skips Part B. long_trails>0 runs the many-escapes-per-trail trap test (walks without distinguished points, long_len operations each, small R allowed), counting returns across escapes against the self-collision expectation; long_escape_add=true runs the rejected additive escape as a control.
